source_text: psa brevis admonitio, subinferens: "Concupiscentiae naturalis qui modum tenet bono bene utitur; qui modum non tenet, bono male utitur; qui autem etiam ipsum modum sanctae virginitatis amore contempserit bono melius non utitur; confidentia quippe suae salutis et roboris, contempsit remedia, ut gloriosa posset exercere certamina
pass_a_gloss: Psa brevis admonitio, subinferens: " of-desire natural who modum holds to-good well utitur; who modum not holds, to-good badly utitur; who however also itself modum sanctae virginitatis amore contempserit to-good melius not utitur; confidentia indeed his-own of-salvation and roboris, contempsit remedia, so-that/as gloriosa would-be-able exercere certamina.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: I will give a brief reminder, so that what has been argued throughout the book may remain in the reader’s heart.

Whoever keeps natural desire within its proper measure uses a good thing well. Whoever does not keep within its measure uses a good thing badly. Whoever, out of love for holy virginity, has renounced even that proper measure does better by not using a good thing. Confident of their health and strength, they have rejected remedies so that they may engage in glorious contests.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
